text.p: Bonds closed easier but prices resisted better than those in Spain. A relative lack of paper was seen continuing to limit the selling pressure.
"We slipped because Spain eased but the futures and the cash markets are not ready to fall as much as the (Spanish) bonos," said one trader.
Another trader saw technical support for the futures at around 106.75 and then if that broke, at 106.50. Resistance was seen at 107.00.
Traders said that the market was supported by the belief that rates could still fall further in Portugal.
"The periphery markets still have room to cut and the Bank of Portugal could do it this month," said one trader.
